top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards one concrete idea, the magic-wavelength optical lattice, which cancels the light shift and removes Doppler and recoil effects for thousands of neutral atoms, with a clean two-name allocation (Katori for the concept and first demonstration, Ye for the record accuracy and many-body clock work). The 1e-18 performance has been reproduced and compared across several independent laboratories, and it has opened new measurements such as millimetre-scale redshift and constant-drift and dark-matter searches. The 2005 and 2012 overlap is answered if the citation names the magic-wavelength lattice rather than clocks in general. P002 is a serious second choice, since an unexpected phase appearing at a predicted angle is the kind of discovery I value, but the interpretation and pairing mechanism are unsettled and the three-name credit is messier after only eight years. An award in a mature, verified field is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: Long-standing collaboration with Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and the Lund and Keller attosecond groups, none of whom is credited in P001 or P002; my field (atomic physics) is close to the lattice clock, but I have no known tie to Katori or Ye, so no recusal is apparent.
